content:
incident-bot: [PAGER] elevated 5xx ratio on /v1/chat/stream (hosted-prod). Rolling error rate ~9% over 10m, spike correlates with cache miss surge. Please triage. Sev: P3.

 taylor: taking. seeing spike in failed token requests. No deploys in last 45m.

 raj: Looking at cache metrics -> prefix-local.hit_rate down from 92% -> 60% over ~12m. Eviction rate increased too. Which cache layer affected?

 nina: Confirmed: local-kv (inference edge) eviction storm started at 15:04 UTC on pool=prefix-kv-edge. cache-bot shows most evicted keys are short prefixes.

 cache-bot: evictions.alert: pool=prefix-kv-edge evictions_per_min=410 (baseline 18). Top-evicted-prefixes: ["how to","play","what is"] (sampled).

 ben: That matches reports of regen loops for short prompts. Could be the new LRU tweak from yesterday's runtime roll.

 taylor: Can someone roll back the LRU change? If it's causing churn we should revert to previous policy.

 raj: Before rollback, quick mitigation: increase local cache size for prefix-kv-edge and temporarily disable aggressive sampling. Patching config now.

 nina: Pushing config patch:
```yaml
pool: prefix-kv-edge
cache:
  mode: keep-hot-keys
  max_entries: 300000
  reserve: 120000
  sample_rate: 0.05  # reduce sampling to avoid evicting hottest prefixes
```

 taylor: Also enabling a soft-fail routing policy: non-critical queries go to cold-capacity to reduce pressure on model pool. ops-bot applying.

 ops-bot: Routing policy change applied -> non-critical->cold-capacity. Rolling update frontends.

 cache-bot: New hit_rate (1m): 84% (up from 60%). Evictions: 32/min.

 taylor: Errors dropping to 3.7%, latency back within 1.4x SLA. Good. Will watch for 30m and then roll revert if stable.

 ben: Post-incident notes: our current alerting is too binary. The eviction alert triggers on absolute >400/min and pages SRE, which is noisy during rollout windows. Need smarter alerts: relative-change, hit-rate drop, and anomaly detector.

 raj: Agreed. Proposed alert set:
- prefix_kv_hit_rate_drop: fire if hit_rate < 0.78 for 5m AND drop of >= 12% compared to 30m moving average. Notify eng-oncall channel. Page only if client error rate >1% or p95 latency >2x SLA.
- prefix_kv_eviction_spike: fire if evictions_per_min > max(200, 3x baseline) for 5m. Inform cache team (no immediate page). Escalate to SRE if persists 20m.
- prefix_kv_top_evicted_keys: low-severity alert that posts top evicted prefixes to channel when top-n changes by >20% in 10m (helps detect rollout-induced pattern).

 nina: Suggested PromQLs for panels/alerts:
```
# 1m hit rate
sum(rate(local_kv_hit_total{pool="prefix-kv-edge"}[1m]))
/
sum(rate(local_kv_requests_total{pool="prefix-kv-edge"}[1m]))

# evictions per minute
sum(increase(local_kv_evictions_total{pool="prefix-kv-edge"}[1m]))

# 30m baseline (for relative change)
sum(rate(local_kv_hit_total{pool="prefix-kv-edge"}[30m]))/
sum(rate(local_kv_requests_total{pool="prefix-kv-edge"}[30m]))
```

 taylor: Good. Also add dashboard annotations when cache policy toggles or routing diversions happen. That made root-cause easier to see.

 ben: I will open GH issues:
- GH#7701: Add relative-change hit-rate alert + page routing rules.
- GH#7702: Grafana dashboard: prefix-kv-edge (1m/5m/15m hit rates, evictions, top-evicted prefixes table, annotations + seed-script run counter).
- GH#7703: Runbook: steps to mitigate eviction storms (TTL bump, disable sampling, route low-pri traffic, seed-hot-keys).

 raj: Quick tactical: adding a lightweight seed script to warm top 50k prefixes from hot-keys store. Running now.

 nina: Seed run started (seed-job/seed-prefixes-2026-03-15T15:22). Progress: 12k/50k seeded; will monitor.

 cache-bot: seed-job completed in 6m. Added 52,100 prefixes. Cache hit warmup observed +6% overall in 10m.

 taylor: Monitoring window green for 25m. Handing to next on-call, @ben, in ~20m.

 ops-bot: Reminder: scheduled handoff in 20m.

 ben: Happy to pick up. Will follow up on GH issues and tune alerts with SRE. Suggest we temporarily lower eviction alert sensitivity for 36h while we observe after changes.

 nina: Also recommend adding a light ML-based anomaly alert on hit_rate using historical seasonality so we don't wake for normal diurnal dips.

 taylor: Agree. For customer impact: ~3k failed requests over 18m window, mostly low-priority chat streams; no pager-facing SLA breach. Support notified to expect a few tickets.

 incident-bot: Incident status -> resolved. No active pages for 30m.

 ben: I'll draft postmortem with timeline + the three GH tasks. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
